specification_compliance: R2-1 is addressed. TranscriptSection.tsx:605-608 now returns early on `!following`, and `following` is in the dependency list, so the reveal that runs when the playback highlight reaches the selected row no longer scrolls a list whose following is suspended. This matches B1 (closing the dialog does not resume following) and the panel's rule that the reader's own scroll wins.

The tap path still reveals the strip. seekTo sets following to true (TranscriptSection.tsx:822), and the reveal driven by revealPendingRef (591-595) never checks `following`, so F4 (no media controller, where seekTo returns early without resuming following) still brings the strip into view after a tap.
R2-2 is addressed. TranscriptSectionTouch.test.tsx now asserts that `fireEvent.keyDown(field, { key: 'Enter' })` returns false, which pins the preventDefault at TranscriptEditDialog.tsx:180.

The new e2e test (transcript-touch.spec.ts, 'with following suspended, playback returning to the selected row does not scroll the list') would kill the mutant that removes `!following`. The fixture's long row (2,000 characters) means following to the last row leaves row 5s above the view. Without the guard, revealCue would move the list by `viewTop - rect.top`, the target's y would change, and the toBeCloseTo(before, 0) check would fail.

I1-I9 are unchanged from r2: the strip is gated on `isSelected`, which requires `coarse`; the fine-path controls are gated on `!coarse`; the dialog captures expected_text and expected_start when it opens; `saving` blocks save, close and Escape; the field is readOnly while saving; and the panel error is hidden while editTarget is set (TranscriptSection.tsx:1110).
The reviewed commit 1e08ae53 changes documentation only. The product delta since r2 is the addon bump in 3da286167.
potential_unspecified_behavior: addons/intelligence/app/main.py:61-63 still sets the service-wide `pdfminer` logger to ERROR. This is r1 TP-1, it is still in the diff, and no spec in this review covers it.
regression_risks: `following` is now a dependency of the reveal effect, so the effect also runs when 再生位置に戻る (resumeFollowing) or a tap sets `following` back to true while the playing row is the selected row. The follow effect (557-560) starts a smooth scrollTo that centres the row. The reveal effect then runs in the same commit and, if the block is not yet fully visible, writes scrollTop directly. In Chromium that can cut the smooth scroll short, leaving the row and strip at the list's edge instead of centred. The row stays visible, so I11 still holds; only the scroll's resting place differs.

If every source becomes empty while the dialog is open, `if (loading || !hasAnything) return null` (TranscriptSection.tsx:1038) unmounts the dialog without clearing editTarget, so it could reappear from the stored text after a later reload. This was raised in r2 and is unchanged; the `last_utterance` guard makes it unlikely.
The new e2e test depends on smooth-scroll settling (it polls every 150ms, then waits a fixed 500ms) and could be timing-sensitive on a slow CI runner.
